title: Debugging Java Programs
learningObjectives: Reproduce a defect reliably before attempting a correction
Isolate the smallest operation that causes the failure
Inspect variable values and the active method call stack
Use breakpoints, stepping and assertions during debugging
Verify each correction with focused regression tests

understand.concept: Debugging is a repeatable process: reproduce, isolate, observe, hypothesize, change one thing and verify. IDE breakpoints pause execution so you can inspect variables and the call stack. Temporary tracing must not expose secrets.
understand.whyItMatters: Debugging Java Programs helps learners create Java applications that are easier to reason about, test and maintain. It connects core language knowledge with realistic programming tasks.
understand.analogy: Treat this concept as a clearly labeled tool: select it for a specific responsibility and check the result.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a learning aid; actual behavior is defined by Java language rules and API contracts.

explain.narrative:
## Debugging as a repeatable investigation

Debugging starts with a reproducible failure, not a guess. Record the input, expected result, actual result and exact steps that trigger the defect. Reduce the case until the smallest failing operation remains; this isolates the cause and removes unrelated distractions.

## Observe execution with an IDE debugger

Set a breakpoint where the result first becomes incorrect. Use step over to run the current line, step into to enter a called method, and step out to finish the current method. Inspect local variables, expressions and the call stack. The call stack shows the active chain of method calls and helps locate where an unexpected value was introduced. A watch expression follows a value as execution proceeds.

## Use tracing and assertions carefully

A temporary log statement can reveal values in a repeatable run, but remove noisy diagnostic output after the cause is understood. Never log passwords, access tokens, private records or other secrets. Assertions express internal assumptions during development; enable them with `-ea`. Assertions are not a substitute for validating user input because they may be disabled.

## Fix one cause and prove the correction

Change one thing at a time. Re-run the smallest reproducing case, then run regression tests for normal, boundary and failure inputs. A fix is not complete merely because one example works: confirm the original failure is gone and nearby behavior has not regressed.

examples.title: Core concept
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int price = 12, quantity = 3; System.out.println("trace: price=" + price + ", quantity=" + quantity); System.out.println(price * quantity); } }
examples.explanation: Adds a focused trace before a calculation so the observed inputs can be checked.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int[] values = {4, 8, 12}; int index = 1; System.out.println("index=" + index + ", length=" + values.length); System.out.println(values[index]); } }
examples.explanation: Prints the index and array length before access, making bounds assumptions visible.

examples.title: Edge case
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int target = 15; int total = 0; for (int n : new int[]{3, 5, 7}) { total += n; System.out.println("after " + n + ": " + total); } System.out.println("target reached=" + (total == target)); } }
examples.explanation: Traces state changes after each loop iteration.

examples.title: API behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { int age = 20; assert age >= 0 : "age must not be negative"; System.out.println("age=" + age); } }
examples.explanation: Demonstrates an assertion for an internal invariant; run with -ea to enable assertions.

examples.title: Test and verify
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { String status = "OPEN"; if (!status.equals("OPEN")) { throw new IllegalStateException("Unexpected status"); } System.out.println("status verified"); } }
examples.explanation: Uses an explicit condition to verify an assumption before proceeding.

practise.guidedTask: Set a breakpoint before a calculation; predict the values, step through each statement, and record the call stack and variable values.
practise.independentTask: Reproduce an off-by-one bug in an array search. Isolate it, correct it, then add tests for first, last, missing and empty cases.
hints: Reproduce the same input and steps before changing code; record expected and actual results.
Use breakpoints, step controls, variable inspection and the call stack to find where a value first becomes incorrect.
After one focused fix, rerun the reproducing case and regression tests; never log credentials or private data.
practise.challenge: Compare a temporary trace statement with an IDE breakpoint. Remove diagnostic output after verification and rerun the regression tests.
